paragraphs: Rabbi Yochanan the scribe of Gufta.

In the Jerusalem Talmud, Sukkah ch. 2, halakhah 5: Rabbi China went to Ein Tav for the sanctification of the new moon, and he was thirsty, until he came to a sukkah of Rabbi Yochanan the scribe of Gufta.

And in Megillah ch. 3, halakhah 7, it states: Rabbi Yochanan the scribe of Gufta went down (it should say: went up) to the Land of Israel and saw Bar Avuna the scribe reading the Song of the Well. And in Tractate Soferim ch. 12, halakhah 4, the reading is: Rabbi Yonatan the scribe of Gufta came down here, etc.
But this is not the one mentioned in the Jerusalem Talmud at the beginning of 'Bameh Behemah' in the name of Chanan of Gufta, as explained in his entry.

notes.text: Yohanan/Yonatan and “went down”/“went up” are retained as the reported readings and Hyman’s correction. The entry expressly distinguishes this figure from Chanan of Gufta.

Guggenheimer Sukkah 2:5 names Rav Huna as the thirsty traveller to Ein Tav and Yochanan the scribe of Gufta as the sukkah’s owner. Hyman’s supplied China and his Yochanan/Yonatan and down/up readings are preserved as distinct reports. This witness does not settle those variants or merge Chanan of Gufta with this figure.
